comparator.name: Human Movement Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: The 180 EC curriculum has a common first year, specialist study in years two and three, a 15 EC minor and a 20 EC graduation project. The 2 EC Bachelor Monitor spans years two and three and counts once.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Six courses (45 EC) differ in each direction. The measurement plan develops numerical modeling, signal processing and computer vision. The health and behavior plan adds clinical psychology, metabolism and qualitative inquiry into people’s experiences.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two coherent related options cover neural control, body function and health research. They differ by 45 EC in each direction and lead to different academic emphases. A dedicated sport-performance plan needs sustained training in exercise testing, biomechanics and performance analysis.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Groningen introduces research questions and professional practice in movement science. UCR’s Personal & Professional Development covers general academic skills.
Groningen studies physical activity and prevention. UCR approaches prevention through population health and epidemiology.
Both use anatomical evidence to link body structure and function. Groningen concentrates on the musculoskeletal system.
Groningen studies diseases that affect movement. UCR covers a wider range of disease mechanisms.
Both study human physiology, including breathing, circulation, and regulation of body systems.
Groningen applies psychology to sport and exercise. UCR focuses on health behavior, prevention and coping with illness.
Groningen applies mechanics to human movement.
Groningen tests bodily responses to exercise. UCR studies exercise as one topic within general physiology.
Groningen designs and evaluates interventions for specific groups.
Choose an eligible minor, placement or period of study abroad.
Groningen covers neuronal function and the sensory and motor systems. UCR introduces neurobiology and brain function.
Both examine how sensory information guides movement and action.
Both study the brain systems involved in attention, memory and higher-order behavior.
Both introduce psychological theories of behavior. UCR also introduces the neural systems behind behavior.
Groningen studies how motor skills develop and are learned. UCR studies broader psychomotor and cognitive development across the lifespan.
Groningen studies models of how the nervous system controls movement.
Groningen examines theoretical and philosophical questions about movement science.
Groningen studies the anatomy of neural systems relevant to movement.
Groningen builds on neuroanatomy to explain motor behavior.
Groningen connects the mechanics of movement with neural control.
Groningen develops practical movement measurement and analysis. UCR teaches image processing and feature tracking.
Both develop programming skills for later analysis. Groningen uses movement data and UCR teaches general programming in Python.
Both develop mathematical tools for scientific problem-solving. Groningen applies them to human movement.
Groningen uses movement measurements in practical work. UCR studies general signal-processing tools.
Groningen designs and analyzes movement experiments. UCR studies probability, inference and simulation.
Both develop experimental design and statistics for research with human participants.
Groningen applies descriptive and inferential statistics to movement research.
Groningen develops statistical analysis and reporting for movement research.
Groningen introduces fields of movement research and professional practice.
Groningen uses specialist equipment to collect and process movement data.
This 2 EC component runs across years two and three.
Groningen requires a 20 EC research project. The optional UCR research element is shown separately.

notes.text: Groningen builds a specialist sequence in biomechanics, exercise testing and movement analysis, followed by a 20 EC research project. The UCR options combine related study of anatomy, neuroscience and health with different research methods.

audience.programmeDescription: This Dutch-taught degree studies how people move, how movement changes with health and age, and how researchers can measure and improve it.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Groningen combines the science of movement with specialist laboratory and research training. The UCR options emphasize measurement and neuroscience or health and behavior.
